registry.description: Doubt is the inner state of being pulled in two directions at once — unable to settle fully on trust or disbelief, confident and uncertain at the same moment. The Greek vocabulary here covers both the act of judging (weighing the evidence) and the genuine uncertainty that remains unsettled. Scripture distinguishes doubt from unbelief: Thomas doubts but is not condemned; the disciples doubt but are sent. Doubt in Scripture is often the companion of genuine faith rather than its opposite — the honest wrestling of a person who is trying to trust in the face of difficulty.
